responses.testimonial:
When I reflect on my leadership journey, I recognize that I lost so much of myself in the collective identity of the feminist movement. The decision to go to Cavite, to attend AktivAsia's FAL Training, was my conscious and defiant act towards healing — of challenging systemic norms and the internalized patriarchy that has in many ways caused a huge deal of hurt to me and other women as well.

During the training, I quieted my racing mind by turning off all the buttons telling me the "shoulds" of my life and the "hows" of being a feminist leader. I was given the space to name my experience and to once again find myself in a healthy sisterhood.

With the women in the training, I regained a renewed feminist spirit. And suddenly, it's like how I started when I was thirteen years old and fully in awe of the world.

responses.next_workshop_suggestion: It would be beneficial to provide reading materials in advance to enhance the understanding of Adaptive Leadership.
responses.testimonial: Attending this training has been an incredibly empowering experience. It provided a safe community where I could openly discuss my challenges as a woman. The unique opportunity to 'step onto the balcony' allowed me to observe the changing landscapes of our world and engage in meaningful discussions on adaptive leadership without the pressure of finding immediate right answers. This experience encouraged me to envision a constructive future where I can apply my experimental methods to navigate uncertain situations. The sense of camaraderie and understanding among participants created an enriching environment for personal and professional growth. I highly recommend this training to anyone looking to enhance their leadership skills and build a supportive network of like-minded individuals.

impact_evaluation_feedback.training_name: Regional Campaign Strategy and Organising Training (CSO)

responses.training_influence: The training helped me slow down and think more deliberately about power, strategy, and the people involved. Before the training, much of my campaigning work was driven by urgency and instinct. After the training, I approach campaigns with a clearer intent. I also prefer people who are passionate rather than filling out profiles.
responses.what_shared:
Over the past few months, I have had the opportunity to share these learnings more formally with students and young campaigners through structured sessions and bootcamps. These spaces focused on campaign thinking, collective power, and storytelling rooted in lived realities. Alongside this, I have continued to share and embed the learnings within my own organization, which has grown since the training, allowing these practices to shape how we plan, communicate, and organize our work. The training tools have become part of our internal culture rather than one off lessons. Some examples of this work can be seen here:
https://www.linkedin.com/posts/parindey_jaarifellowship-womenpeacebuilders-feministdialogue-activity-7361089306528026625-HHXk
https://www.linkedin.com/posts/syeda-kashmala-758a9aa3_spark360-bootcamp-youth-activity-7371961954946473985-Kjf5
responses.whats_alive: My current focus is on climate justice, renewable energy transitions, and the intersection of climate change with human rights. I am also working on digital rights and freedom of expression, particularly for journalists, women, and marginalized communities, utilizing storytelling and legal advocacy as complementary tools for organizing and driving change.
responses.testimonial:
Yessssssss,

The training helped me shift from always reacting to crises to campaigning with intention and strategy. It gave me practical tools to think about power, storytelling, and collective action, while also reminding me that care and sustainability are not add ons but core to the work. What stayed with me most was the sense of shared learning and solidarity. In spaces where campaigning can feel isolating and risky, that feeling of not doing the work alone really matters. The relationships and frameworks I gained continue to inform how I design campaigns, mentor younger organizers, and build movements that are grounded, resilient, and led by people rather than pressure.
responses.anything_else: The training created a rare space where learning felt collective rather than competitive. That sense of solidarity matters deeply in regions where campaigning can often feel isolating. Recently, I unexpectedly met Francis son at the Asia Energy Transition Summit in Pakistan, and that moment instantly brought back how meaningful our work together had been. It was a quiet reminder that these connections stay with you, long after the training ends. Maintaining and nurturing these relationships is just as important as the skills themselves. Even a yearly continuity space or gathering would help sustain motivation and reaffirm that we are not working in isolation, but as part of a shared and ongoing movement.
responses.need_support: Support around advanced campaign strategy, regional collaboration, and mentoring for younger campaigners would be valuable. There is also strong scope to co develop issue based trainings on climate justice, organizing in restrictive civic spaces, which I would be interested in leading with AktivAsia’s support. Alongside this, I am also engaged in campaigning for digital rights and data protection through a gendered lens, particularly as digital harms increasingly intersect with climate, civic participation, and organizing spaces. If of interest, there is potential to thoughtfully integrate this perspective into climate-focused campaigning work as well.
responses.key_focus: Context-specific campaign trainings on digital surveillance and political risk are most needed. Trainings that combine strategy, care, and sustainability for campaigners, while remaining grounded in local political realities, would be especially impactful at the sub-national level.

Campaign is about creating a comprehensive strategy that filled by tactics and everything that I need to achieve the objective. So, it makes a phase to phase situation for me to create & implement a campaign.

In my previous organization (KontraS), I've tried to socialize how important the Theory of Change is. There's also huge problem about a different positioning and definition of campaign in my organization. Campaign was treated only as the mobilization part of works. It's only about public opinion & participation. Campaign in my organization could be placed in the last step after research & advocacy stuff. And it's different with something that I know before and become stronger after I joined their training, campaign is the umbrella of any tactics that should be done, including research & advocacy.

So there's only a lil moment for me to share about the Theory of Change & tactics as a way to fill the programs in our annual meeting.

아시아의 멋진 여성활동가들을 만날 수 있는 소중한 기회였습니다. 20대부터 60대까지 다양한 연령과 다양한 의제를 가진 각국의 여성활동가들로부터 지혜와 경험을 통해 자매애를 나눌 수 있었습니다. 특별히, 첫날밤과 이튿날의 세션으로 우리는 굉장히 비슷한 경험들과 어려움을 가지고 있다는 것, 또한 같은 희망을 품고 있다는 것을 발견할 수 있었습니다. 또한 '리더'에 대해 다시 생각해보며, 우리조직과 한국에 있는 문제들과 이를 위해 필요한 적응적 해결방식에 대한 고민들을 가지게 했습니다.
the program make you think again about lead which make you pressure and hurt. So the training make you freedom woman
The training was a moment of learning and unlearning and yes, being comfortable sitting with the discomfort of what was shared that "leader" is a patriarchal construct.

I am facing a hard time in my organization on the practice of leadership of my leader. Because of that, I feel that I have to bring all the expectation from the staff to me. And this training makes me realize that is no perfect leader and do not drown in people’s expectation.

Besides, the practice of leadership (observe, interpret, intervene), helps me a lot to erase my bias and important to know the perspective of other people.
Yes, i hope this training can touch community esspesially  and we have  many stakeholder to join this program because so interested

Leadership, as we know it, has been interrogated and assessed through a feminist lens that ,on one hand, recognizes its present power structure, but also identifies ways to observe, orient, decide, and, act on it. It gave a fresh perspective on the critical questions it takes in order to thrive in a leadership position yet ensuring that we, as women, are as empowered as we can get to survive the process.

This training helped interrogate some of my internalized beliefs about leadership and feminism - a process that is usually difficult when one is so involved or holds high expectations from a particular system, or when one's passion tends to drown the sound of other perspectives.  This space - Feminist Adaptive Training - listens to intergenerational voices, the said and unsaid; allows critical opinions and affirms the "I" unapologetically.

The training is very timely in today's challenges as a women who lead a team when facing facist and dictatorial leaderships we have been expirencing globally. The feminist adaptative leadership is very empowering and affirming to us.

When I reflect on my leadership journey, I recognize that I lost so much of myself in the collective identity of the feminist movement. The decision to go to Cavite, to attend AktivAsia's FAL Training, was my conscious and defiant act towards healing — of challenging systemic norms and the internalized patriarchy that has in many ways caused a huge deal of hurt to me and other women as well.

During the training, I quieted my racing mind by turning off all the buttons telling me the "shoulds" of my life and the "hows" of being a feminist leader. I was given the space to name my experience and to once again find myself in a healthy sisterhood.

With the women in the training, I regained a renewed feminist spirit. And suddenly, it's like how I started when I was thirteen years old and fully in awe of the world.

This training really helped me to navigate and understand how our organization works using the lens of adaptive leadership. With this information, I feel empowered to leverage it as a competitive edge to survive in the system.

Attending this training has been an incredibly empowering experience. It provided a safe community where I could openly discuss my challenges as a woman. The unique opportunity to 'step onto the balcony' allowed me to observe the changing landscapes of our world and engage in meaningful discussions on adaptive leadership without the pressure of finding immediate right answers. This experience encouraged me to envision a constructive future where I can apply my experimental methods to navigate uncertain situations. The sense of camaraderie and understanding among participants created an enriching environment for personal and professional growth. I highly recommend this training to anyone looking to enhance their leadership skills and build a supportive network of like-minded individuals.
